They plan to replace us. We have been the, if you will, the superpower, the hyper-power, all in the collapse of the Iron Curtain, and they want to assume that position. I think they would look for an authoritarian world where they basically dictate to the world what the conditions are for economic trade and the like. And so that's a pretty frightening objective on their part. And my view is that the nations of the rest of the world, the West Democratic nations, nations that follow the rule of law, that those nations need to come together and say, wait a second, what are the rules going to be that we're going to live by? And we would have to deny to China the right to have access to our markets so they don't play by those rules. And it is my hope that if we're successful in doing that as a group of ourselves coming together and developing those rules that the China would be dissuaded from a course of confrontation and instead play a more collaborative, competitive role in the geopolitical marketplace.

turn_text: It's pretty straightforward in a setting like impeachment where having already sworn an oath to defend the Constitution as a Senator, we were required to swear an additional oath when the impeachment trial occurred. And the Chief Justice of the United States in the first case, and then the President Pro Tem in the second case administered a new oath of office where we swore to apply impartial justice, so help us God. And at that point, when you swear to apply impartial justice, that suggests that you're not going to be partial to a team or a party or even a personal relationship. It's impartial. And you're going to try and do what is in your judgment, the right thing. So for me, that's pretty straightforward that in a circumstance like that you are you're swearing before God to put Your your conscience and which you think is right above all above all else There are other circumstances where where you say let's say in a policy matter, which is that should we adjust a a tax for instance You say okay, you know, I don't like that tax, but I do like what our our group of people is doing generally So I'm gonna work with them on this one and help them on this, but even though I don't like it very much, it's not a matter of principle, I just don't like it much. And because I think in the long run, we can work together on something I like better. I mean, that's the nature of saying, how do you get things done that conforms with what your view would be? I mean, you don't want to be oppositional on everything that you have any disagreement with. There are some people, by the way, that want to fight every single thing they don't agree with 100%. They don't get much done. So I'd like to say, could I agree with elements in a proposal?
